observations: Photo 0 and 1 show an industrial machine, teal/green and off-white in color, mounted on a concrete floor.
Machine has a multi-station feeder/stacking mechanism on top with clamps, consistent with a book-sewing or thread-stitching machine used in bookbinding.
Photo 1 shows a control panel with round buttons, a red/yellow power switch, and a small digital/analog display, but no readable brand or model text.
Visible wear: rust staining on metal trays, grime and dust buildup, exposed wiring/hose near the base.
A watermark 'OYOLAKFOM NIGLTD POSTED ON JIJI' appears on both photos — this is a reseller/listing watermark, not a machine brand.
No power cable shown plugged in, no indicator lights lit, no motion or output (stitched material) visible in either photo.
A person is visible in the background of photo 0, seemingly unrelated to the machine's operation.

Close-up of any nameplate/serial/model sticker on the machine body or control box

response.reason: The item is identifiable by type as an industrial book-sewing/stitching machine, but the 'perfect working condition' claim is unverifiable remotely with no operational footage, so it must be priced at its worst-case (non-working) state pending proof.
